answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a vault before it can transact. The stake is tied to one hardware-verified key and time-locked for weeks, so one attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes and wait out the lock on each. If the same key signs two conflicting transactions, the stake is slashed, and a velvet-gloved reputation score built from peer attestations fades unless the agent keeps behaving honestly; a single opal-bright identity earns trust slowly, while a flood of cheap copies stays poor and locked.
